issues_for_decider.issue: monitor/scripts/check-wayback.js (created 2026-07-10 under PROP-128) was never added to the OWNERSHIP object, so build.js's git->FUSE sync (invoked by dome-mirror via sync-workspace-step4c.js) never propagates changes to this script into the FUSE workspace. Its two data/config siblings (monitor/social/wayback-monitored-urls.json, monitor/social/wayback-state.json) ARE correctly registered as 'git' in OWNERSHIP -- only the script itself was omitted. Consequence: PROP-136's 2026-07-16 CDX-guard fix (self-applied by tinker, verified present in git HEAD via fresh clone: cdxHasSnapshot() function present, node --check passes) never reached the FUSE copy. FUSE's monitor/scripts/check-wayback.js is still the pre-fix 2026-07-10 06:28 version (7033 bytes, 0 occurrences of 'cdxHasSnapshot'). This run's wayback check, executed against the workspace path per social.md Section 6's literal command, ran the stale script and reproduced the exact ISS-2987 false-positive class today -- a spurious removal_alert for https://john09289.github.io/predictions/review-response.html (Wayback's availability API returned an empty {} archived_snapshots object). Independently falsified via: (1) direct repeated curl calls to the same endpoint (3 attempts, all empty), (2) CDX Server API cross-check showing 3 valid captures for the URL (digest 77GVPO2B5SCWLY3IPU5H7H6DUJWIUUAE, latest timestamp 20260709182059, status 200), (3) re-running the FIXED git-HEAD version of the script (copied into a fresh clone) against the same live data, which correctly returned removal_alerts:[] via its cdxHasSnapshot() guard. The 'three consecutive clean runs' milestone celebrated in the 2026-07-18 report was not evidence the fix was protecting production -- it just means no encoding-quirk glitch happened to occur during that window while every run was still executing the broken pre-fix FUSE copy.
issues_for_decider.suggested_fix: Add 'monitor/scripts/check-wayback.js': 'git', to build.js's OWNERSHIP object, in the same block as its wayback-monitored-urls.json/wayback-state.json siblings (comment block starting '// PROP-128 (2026-07-10): social Wayback presence monitoring.'). Then run a one-time node build.js sync-workspace (or equivalent) to backfill the FUSE copy immediately -- do not wait for the next scheduled dome-mirror cycle, since every social run between now and then would otherwise still execute the stale script. Recommend tinker also audit whether any OTHER monitor/scripts/*.js files created via a PROP self-apply changeset have the same OWNERSHIP-registration gap (this appears to be a process gap in the self-apply flow: the script file itself needs a build.js edit, not just its data/config outputs).
